additional_concerns: The transition provision preserves processing of existing applications. It does not expressly establish permanent substantive ineligibility for the underlying change. The legacy exclusions in node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 remain proposed interpretations, especially after a subsequent decision, withdrawal or resubmission.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question rather than resolving their eligibility. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa tests substantive conditions only. Their results are not interchangeable with actual procedural availability of relief.

The explicit commencement date supports dated assessment, but does not independently establish implementation date as the controlling event for every transitional case. Node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e requires clarification on this point.

The publication date needed to reconcile immediate effect with 28 November 2025 is absent. The relevant FAQs and any SFC clarification of transitional availability are also absent; the supplied missing dependency IDs have no identifying mapping, so neither can safely be assigned to these authorities.

The introductory reference to home-regulator supervision describes the measures' purpose. Item (ii) expressly requires home-jurisdiction compliance; importing item (i)'s separate supervision condition into item (ii) is not established.

Novelty, complexity, possible local policy implications and home compliance remain supplied legal or factual judgments. The formulas preserve their logical roles but do not establish those classifications or overall compliance.
